_about: Convair 580 (CVLT), step 1 of 2: the Convair 340 airframe it's converted from, read off the three views in the USAF technical order T.O. 1C-131B-2-2, page 2B (the C-131B Samaritan, a 340 airframe with R-2800 radials), as uploaded to Wikimedia Commons (File:Convair C-131B Samaritan 3-view line drawing.png: a 1850 x 2408 px greyscale scan, public domain as a USAF work). Rasterized with layers.py --mode image --threshold 170: the side at scale 3; the plan, drawn nose down, turned nose left and evened out lengthwise (--xscale 1.0525, drawn 5% short); the front at 3.0214 (side.anchors.json, plan.anchors.json, front.anchors.json). Scaled by the printed 79 ft 2 in (24.13 m) overall length between its extension lines at the nose tip and the tail cone (68, 3468.5 px). The C-131B's nacelles, propellers, square windows and cargo door aren't the 580's: they're placeholders here (the propeller's plane and hub from the drawing's three-bladed one, no windows or doors). Step 2, derive.py, writes the 580 over this from photo.json: the longer radar nose, the enlarged fin, the Allison nacelles and four-bladed propellers, the cabin windows, doors and flight-deck glass. The tailplane is drawn edge on in the side view 0.11 m under the centerline (stabilizerZ 785, its lens's middle at its root); the front view draws it only between the propeller disc and the fuselage.

windows.note: Placeholder: the 580's windows come from derive.py.
